;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**[[2020 Chaman bombing]]
***A motorcycle [[improvised explosive device|bomb]] kills five people and injures 20 others in [[Chaman]], [[Killa Abdullah District|Killa Abdullah]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1573634/at-least-5-killed-20-injured-in-powerful-blast-in-chaman (''Dawn'')]
*[[2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo massacres]]
**Nineteen people are killed in [[massacre]]s in three villages in [[Ituri Province]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/killed-ethnic-violence-eastern-dr-congo-200810150343205.html (Al Jazeera English)]

;Business and economy
*[[McDonald's]] files a [[United States dollar|US$]]40 million lawsuit against former CEO [[Steve Easterbrook]], equal to the worth of his [[severance package]], for allegedly lying to investigators about the extent of his [[sexual relationship]]s with three employees. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/10/business/mcdonalds-steve-easterbrook-ceo-lawsuit/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Toshiba]] exits the [[personal computer]] (PC) market after 35 years, by selling its final stake in PC manufacturer [[Dynabook Inc.]] [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-53721016 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Kerala floods]]
**A [[landslide]] during [[flood]]s at a [[tea plantation]] in [[Kerala]], [[India]], leaves at least 49 people dead. It is feared that many more people are buried under debris. [https://news.sky.com/story/tea-plantation-landslide-kills-49-in-india-as-more-feared-buried-12046440 (Sky News)]
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**[[Prime Minister of Mauritius|Mauritian Prime Minister]] [[Pravind Jugnauth]] warns that the tanker may "break in two" as the country awaits help from other nations that have pledged aid amid a state of emergency. Jugnauth adds the nation lacks the skills and resources needed to relocate the wrecked vessel, and that the nation will likely never recover from the ecological damage done by the spill. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53722701 (BBC News)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mauritius-oil-spill-disaster-satellite-images/ (CBS)]
*[[2020 Volgograd explosion]]
**An explosion at a [[gas station]] in [[Volgograd]], [[Volgograd Oblast]], [[Russia]], injures at least 13 people and creates a {{convert|1000|m2|ft2|abbr=on}}-sized blaze. It is believed that it was caused by an [[electrical fire]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/russia-explosion-volgograd-today-blast-injuries-gas-station-a9663636.html (''The Independent'')]
*A [[gas explosion]] in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]], [[United States]], leaves at least one dead and four injured. Homes were damaged or destroyed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-us-canada-53730171/gas-explosion-destroys-multiple-homes-in-baltimore (BBC News)]
*[[August 2020 Midwest derecho]]
**A powerful [[derecho]] with winds over 100 mph sweeps across the [[Midwestern United States]] and leaves four dead and causes $11 billion [[USD]] in damage. 
;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Guam]]
***[[Guam]] [[Governor of Guam|Governor]] [[Lou Leon Guerrero]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.pacificislandtimes.com/single-post/2020/08/11/Guam-governor-tests-positive-for-Covid-19 (''Pacific Island Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
***Spanish actor [[Antonio Banderas]] announces via Twitter that he has tested positive for COVID-19. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/10/entertainment/antonio-banderas-coronavirus/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**A day after the ''[[loya jirga]]'' approved of the release of "hardcore" [[Taliban]] prisoners, [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] signs the order to release them. Taliban spokesman Suhail Shaheen says the Taliban "is ready" for talks. U.S. Special Envoy [[Zalmay Khalilzad]] welcomed the agreement. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban/afghan-president-signs-off-on-taliban-prisoner-release-peace-talks-expected-in-days-idUSKCN2560DL?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Law and crime
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**[[Hong Kong]] entrepreneur and [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] activist [[Jimmy Lai]] and his son are arrested under the national security law for allegedly conspiring with foreign powers. He is so far the most high-profile figure to be charged under the law. [[Hong Kong Police Force|The police]] also search the offices of his company ''[[Next Digital]]'' shortly after his arrest. Activist [[Agnes Chow]] was also arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/10/hong-kong-media-tycoon-jimmy-lai-arrested-over-alleged-foreign-collusion (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3096679/hong-kong-national-security-law-media-mogul-jimmy-lai (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[Riot]]ing and [[looting]] occurs in [[Chicago]], U.S., after a [[Chicago Police Department|police]] shooting. Thirteen police officers are injured, two people are shot, and more than 100 are arrested. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/breaking/ct-chicago-downtown-looting-20200810-3zwa3b7zzrc5vdyb4qjqywrjvu-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')]
*A shooting involving the [[United States Secret Service|Secret Service]] occurs on [[Pennsylvania Avenue]] near the [[White House]], [[Washington, D.C.]], U.S. A civilian, identified only as a 51-year-old man, has been transported to a local hospital. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/secret-service-escorts-trump-briefing-room-amid-shooting/story?id=72293741 (ABC News)]
*A [[US Air Force]] [[UH-1N]] is shot at near [[Manassas]], [[Virginia]], injuring one of two pilots while flying ten miles northwest of Manassas on a training mission at an altitude of 1,000 feet. It lands safely at [[Manassas Regional Airport]] west of [[Washington, DC]], and the pilot is taken to hospital where they are treated and released. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/12/politics/fbi-investigating-air-force-helicopter-shooting/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian presidential election]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**During the second day of protests across [[Belarus]], police fire [[rubber bullet]]s to disperse protesters in the capital [[Minsk]], wounding a journalist. About 30 people are arrested in the city; some protestors were beaten by police. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53721410 (BBC News)]
**A protester in Minsk is killed after being shot by police officers. It is the first death during the protests. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/15/people-of-minsk-bid-farewell-to-protester-killed-in-post-election-unrest (Euronews)]
*[[2020 Trinidad and Tobago general election]]
**Citizens of [[Trinidad and Tobago]] cast their votes in the country's [[Elections in Trinidad and Tobago|general election]]. [https://www.foreignbrief.com/daily-news/trinidad-and-tobago-to-hold-general-election/ (''Foreign Brief'')]
*[[2019–2020 Lebanese protests]], aftermath of the [[2020 Beirut explosions]]
**[[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Hassan Diab]] announces the [[resignation]] of the entire [[government of Lebanon|government]] as protests grow over their handling of the Beirut explosions on 4 August. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lebanon-security-blast/lebanon-government-resigns-amid-outrage-over-beirut-blast-idUSKCN2560XY?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**The [[Mountain West Conference]] becomes the second [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] league to call off its [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|football season]], as well as all other fall sports. This follows the lead of the [[Mid-American Conference]], which announced an identical plan two days earlier. [https://themw.com/news/2020/8/10/general-mountain-west-postpones-2020-fall-sports.aspx (Mountain West Conference)] [https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/29635064/sources-mountain-west-postpone-fall-sports-season (ESPN)]
